title: On Glancing at the letter on the table
subtitle: 文学写作 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 文学写作（人与社会·文学艺术与体育·文学与写作）
meta: 主题语境：文学写作（人与社会·文学艺术与体育·文学与写作）　|　核心词汇：glance　|　正文 362 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 glance 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1954 the craftsman ① glanced at the letter on the table without a word of thanks, and every apprentice in the workshop said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three years on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the craftsman ② glances at the letter on the table at once without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ glance at the letter on the table at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ glanced at the letter on the table before — a line in the ledger for August 1948 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Glancing at the letter on the table without a word of thanks, the craftsman said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the tool at the far bench, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ glance over the list before signing at once, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Glance over the list before signing at once and never mention it again.

By 1961 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the ledger, and a new apprentice from the next workshop ⑧ glances over the list before signing without a word of thanks every year without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the bench, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ glanced at the letter on the table again when nobody else would.

⑩ To glance at the letter on the table, my mother said in 1966, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the workshop remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the workshop forgets, somebody glances at the letter on the table at once again and somebody must glance at the letter on the table without a word of thanks all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 瞥一眼（一般过去式 glanced at the letter on the table：1954 年匠人头一回这样做，不图一句谢）
B. v. 瞥一眼（一般现在 glances at the letter on the table：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 瞥一眼（不定式 to glance at the letter on the table：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 瞥一眼（过去完成时 had glanced at the letter on the table：1948 年八月的工料簿上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 瞥一眼（动名词 glancing at the letter on the table 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 扫过（glance over the list before signing：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去扫过签字前把那份名单扫一遍）
G. v. 扫过（glance over the list before signing：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 瞥一眼（后段两处：新来的学徒照例 glances over the list before signing，而母亲又一次 glanced at the letter on the table）

glance 意为“瞥一眼”，自那以后匠人二话不说地把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 glances。
glance 意为“瞥一眼”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯瞥一眼瞥了桌上的那封信一眼”，此处为不定式 to glance at the letter on the table。
glance 意为“瞥一眼”，工料簿里 八月 那行字说明早在 1961 年之前就有人瞥一眼过，故用过去完成时 had glanced。

glance 意为“瞥一眼”，新来的学徒每个年头都照例扫过签字前把那份名单扫一遍，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 glances。
glance 意为“瞥一眼”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次不图一句谢瞥一眼瞥了桌上的那封信一眼，用一般过去式 glanced 叙述。
glance 意为“瞥一眼”，结尾那句是母亲 1966 年的话：要瞥一眼瞥了桌上的那封信一眼，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和工坊记住的那一件。

items: 1954 年，匠人不图一句谢瞥一眼瞥了桌上的那封信一眼；工坊里每一个学徒都说这是头一回。（glanced at the letter on the table）

老手们留下的规矩说得明白：立刻扫过签字前把那份名单扫一遍，以后再也不要提起。（glance over the list before signing，祈使句）

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 glance 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1954 the craftsman glanced at the letter on the table without a word of thanks, and nobody in the workshop forgot it.
Even now the craftsman glances at the letter on the table at once whenever the workshop asks.
Glancing at the letter on the table without a word of thanks, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever glance over the list before signing at once, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new apprentice from the next workshop glances over the list before signing without a word of thanks every year, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother glanced at the letter on the table again, and the workshop remembered that half.
